V1.scale: Measured ~150 bytes of stack per nesting level (256 KB probe cap exceeded between 800 and 1600 levels, transition at ~1200 levels). With the evaluation's 1 MB stack and ~80 KB framework overhead, ~944 KB is available for recursion: 944 KB / 150 bytes ≈ 6300 nesting levels to overflow. Densest encoding is fixarray-of-1 (0x91) at 1 byte per level plus 1 terminal byte (0xC0), so about 6300 bytes of input.

V2.scale: Measured 4 bytes of heap per declared array element (Value reference, compressed oops). 256 MB probe cap exceeded at 64M elements. Extrapolating to the evaluation's 1 GB heap with ~150-200 MB JVM overhead: ~200M elements × 4 bytes = 800 MB, exhausting available heap. Input is a 5-byte ARRAY32 header (0xDD + 4-byte big-endian size).

V3.scale: Measured 1 byte of heap per declared payload byte (direct byte array allocation). 256 MB probe cap exceeded at 256M declared bytes. Extrapolating to the evaluation's 1 GB heap with ~150-200 MB JVM overhead: ~800M declared bytes → 800 MB allocated, exhausting available heap. Input is a 5-byte BIN32 header (0xC6 + 4-byte big-endian length).
